Series::antidiff¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::antidiff -> Series::AntidiffAccessor

Series::antidiff() -> SeriesAntidiffProxy
Series::antidiff(const Series& x) -> SeriesAntidiffProxy

What It Does¶

antidiff is a namespace-like accessor for numerical antidifferentiation of an already-sampled Series: composite-trapezoidal integration (trapezoid) and its running form (cumulative_trapezoid), stochastic integrals of sampled values (ito, strat, theta) and quadratic variation and covariation. Like linearalg, it does not compute a value by itself — it selects the method family and keeps the owning Series as the values being integrated.

Why This Has Its Own Accessor¶

The name is deliberate. antidiff is the reverse of Series::diff() (discrete forward differencing, x[i+1] - x[i]): both operate on an already-materialized sequence of numbers, with no reference to any generating function. cumsum(diff(x)) reconstructs x exactly (up to one boundary value); antidiff().cumulative_trapezoid(x) is the same family of operation — a cumulative sum built from consecutive differences — but not the literal same formula, since it weights each term by the trapezoidal rule (approximating an integral) rather than replaying the raw differences.

This is deliberately not a home for continuous integration of an arbitrary callable — pluss::integ::quadra, pluss::integ::aleatoria, and the Analytica closed-form registry (PlussMa) cover that. Those need to re-invoke a function at points they choose themselves; a single already-computed Series cannot provide that, only its own already-sampled values. See trapezoid for the full reasoning.

Calling Styles¶

The dot-style form passes the x-coordinates to individual methods:

auto area = y.antidiff.trapezoid(x);

The proxy style binds the x-coordinates first:

auto area = y.antidiff(x).trapezoid();

Both calls integrate y over x. A third form needs no x-coordinates at all — a uniform spacing dx (default 1.0) is enough:

auto area_default = y.antidiff.trapezoid();      // dx = 1.0
auto area_dx = y.antidiff.trapezoid(0.5);        // dx = 0.5

The zero-argument dot-style form (y.antidiff.trapezoid()) resolves based on whether a peer was bound: with a bound peer (y.antidiff(x).trapezoid()) it integrates against that x; without one, it falls back to dx = 1.0.

Method Pages¶

  • trapezoid: total area under y over x (or a uniform spacing), reduced along one dimension

  • cumulative_trapezoid: the running antiderivative, one value per sample point

Use the Series::AntidiffAccessor API Reference as the landing page for this family.

Returns¶

Series::AntidiffAccessor or SeriesAntidiffProxy A lightweight method-selection object bound to the owning Series, and optionally to a peer Series (the x-coordinates).

Accessing `antidiff` does not copy numeric data and does not mutate the
owner.

Example¶

auto y = pluss::make_series({0.0, 1.0, 4.0, 9.0, 16.0});
auto x = pluss::make_series({0.0, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0});

std::cout << "call_style=" << y.antidiff().trapezoid(x) << "\n";
std::cout << "dot_style=" << y.antidiff.trapezoid(x) << "\n";
std::cout << "peer_bound=" << y.antidiff(x).trapezoid() << "\n";

Output¶

call_style=pluss::Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=22
dot_style=pluss::Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=22
peer_bound=pluss::Series(shape=[], strides=[], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=22

All three spellings integrate the same y over the same x and agree exactly.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • antidiff is an accessor, not a materialized result.

  • The zero-argument dot-style method (y.antidiff.trapezoid()) silently uses dx = 1.0 unless a peer was bound via y.antidiff(x) first — it never throws for “forgetting” x, since dx-only integration is a legitimate, separate calling form, not an error state.

  • trapezoid/cumulative_trapezoid both require x (when given) to be broadcastable against y along the reduced dimension; a genuinely incompatible length throws.
